texts: On day 21 of Year 1, Hesper reported to the Council that the cold snap had cost about one and a half vessels of mire-essence.
Hesper reported to the Council that the salt-bloom store held eight weeks of winter supply.
Brindle Coombe reported to the Council that the Northcove production was normal.
Sailsworn reported to the Council that the next new moon was twelve days away.
Sailsworn reported to the Council that twelve members would form the harvest party.
Old Vesh proposed that Coraline Ash join the salt-bloom harvest party.
The Council agreed that Coraline Ash would join the harvest party.

q1_issues.issue: The scale slot of (Measure sk_mire_essence_1 quantity ...) is filled with 'quantity', which no word in the clause supplies — Measures & units reserves the symbol 'unspecified' for an unstated dimension and says a scale no word supplies is never invented ('duration' at statement 20 is the same borrowing, though a time unit makes it more defensible).

(Past (BeforeBy now sk_new_moon_1 12 day)) wraps a temporal-ordering relation in Past, which Status predicates licenses only over an event witness or a categorical/copular atom, and the reading is incoherent ('it was the case that now is twelve days before the new moon'); the reference point of 'twelve days away' is the day-21 report, not the speech-time constant now.

new_moon is fused as a compound kind but gets none of the decomposition atoms Compound concepts makes mandatory — no genus (Inheritance new_moon moon) and no adjectival modifier genus — while every other compound in this parse (cold_snap, salt_bloom_store, winter_supply, harvest_party, mire_essence, salt_bloom_harvest_party) does get its genus.

q2_gaps: Measure-phrase NPs quantifying a mass noun — 'one and a half vessels of mire-essence', 'eight weeks of winter supply' — have no encoding: Possessive / genitive NP explicitly excludes the measure of-phrase ('a cup of water') but nothing replaces it, and no word supplies a scale for the Measure form the parse fell back on.

A temporal-distance predication inside a seal whose reference point is the matrix event's time ('the next new moon was twelve days away'): ordering atoms may not cross a seal boundary, so the report event cannot anchor it, and the only licensed anchor, the speech-time constant now, is the wrong time.

'next' as a restrictive modifier on an entity NP ('the next new moon') has no licensed carrier — the 'next / last Tuesday' rule covers only time adverbials, where the clause's tense carries the direction.

A mandative subjunctive that-complement ('proposed that Coraline Ash join ...') — a tenseless finite-shaped complement — is not addressed by Propositional attitudes, which assumes a tensed finite clause or a to-infinitive control complement.
review.notes: Seal discipline is handled carefully and correctly throughout: report/propose/agree stay non-factive with Experiencer holders and no top-level predication of P, definite and named typing plus compound genus atoms project while indefinite witnesses and the Northcove Possession stay sealed, and both embedded 'would' complements take (Future e) inside the seal per Sequence of tense. Roles are right too, including Agent on the stative transitive 'held' and Patient on the created harvest party.

issues.reason: Measures & units states that 'a scale no word supplies is never invented — an unstated dimension takes the reserved slot symbol unspecified', and neither 'about one and a half vessels of mire-essence' nor 'eight weeks of winter supply' supplies the words quantity or duration.

The anchor half stands — 'twelve days away' is measured from the day-21 report, so (BeforeBy now sk_new_moon_1 12 day) records a distance from speech time that the text never states (and Past over a now-relation is self-cancelling) — but the licensing half is overstated, since Comparatives & degree explicitly wraps a relation atom from a copular clause in tense ('Alice was taller than Bob' -> (Past (More tall alice bob))).

Compound concepts suppresses the head genus when the IS-A fails ('a hot dog is not a dog'), and 'the next new moon' here denotes a lunar-phase occurrence still twelve days ahead — not a kind of moon, and not a thing of which 'is new' is predicable — so withholding (Inheritance new_moon moon) and the modifier genus is licensed rather than an omission.

gaps_confirmed: Measure-phrase / container of-phrase over a mass noun ('one and a half vessels of mire-essence', 'eight weeks of winter supply') has no licensed encoding: the genitive section excludes the measure 'of' ('a cup of water') and names no replacement, and the Measure fallback has no word to fill its scale slot.

A temporal-distance predication inside a seal whose reference point is the matrix event's time ('the next new moon was twelve days away'): ordering atoms may not cross a seal boundary, so the report event cannot anchor it, and the one licensed anchor (the speech-time constant now) is the wrong time.

'next' as a restrictive modifier on an entity NP ('the next new moon') has no licensed carrier — the 'next / last Tuesday' rule covers only time adverbials, where the clause's tense carries the direction, and Ordinal defines only first / a numeral / last.

A mandative subjunctive that-complement ('proposed that Coraline Ash join …') — a tenseless finite-shaped clause — is not addressed by Propositional attitudes, which assumes either a tensed finite clause or a to-infinitive control complement.
new_gaps: Day-of-year / era dating ('on day 21 of Year 1') has no well-formed term: (Day <n>) is the month-day slot that composes with (Month <name>), so (Day 21) reads as the 21st of an unstated month, and (Year 1) cannot be distinguished from a calendar year.
adjudication.defect_summary: For the confirmed scale issue the compliant form is the reserved slot symbol — (Measure sk_mire_essence_1 unspecified (ParticleFromNormal 1.5 0.15) vessel), and likewise unspecified in place of duration on the supply measure — since no word in either clause supplies a dimension; for the standing half of the partial, NO compliant form is licensed: the distance is anchored on the matrix report's time, ordering atoms may not cross a seal boundary, and now is the only licensed anchor, so the clause should have been left unencoded with the gap recorded (filed above).
adjudication.notes: Seal discipline, holder roles, projection of definite/named typing and compound genus atoms, and the embedded-'would' Future are all correct, so the parse fails on two narrow slot/anchor points rather than on structure. Both failures sit next to genuine coverage gaps, which is where the re-parse instruction set will have to move first.
